title: Expected payoff against a pure column is at most one
statement: Let $G$ be a finite two-player zero-sum game whose payoff matrix $A$ has every entry in $[0,1]$, let $p$ be a mixed row strategy with weights $p_i$, and let $j$ be a fixed pure column action. Then the row player's expected payoff against column $j$ satisfies \[ \sum_i p_i \cdot A_{ij} \;\le\; 1. \]
hypotheses_covered: G is a finite zero-sum game with payoff entries in [0,1]
p is a mixed row strategy (weights nonnegative, summing to one)
j is a fixed pure column action
replaced:
For any game $G$, mixed row strategy $p$, and pure column action $j$,
$\mathrm{payoffVsPure}(G,p,j) \leq 1$.
